historical_pattern.summary: Replay of a captured ciphertext is one of the oldest breaks against messaging protocols: if a receiver accepts the same sealed message twice, an attacker who captured it once can re-deliver it (duplicate actions, forced re-execution, oracle probing). dycrpt carries a ReplayCache precisely to stop this; this campaign attacks that defense directly.

surface.notes: ReplayCache is constructed with capacity 4096 (src/engine/mod.rs:569). The attack tests both a direct re-delivery and a re-delivery after cache pressure (>4096 intervening messages) to probe eviction-based replay.

invariant: A SealedMessage that has already been successfully opened can never be opened a second time to yield its plaintext; the second attempt must return an error and must not return the original plaintext.
attacker_capabilities: can observe and capture ciphertexts on the wire
can re-inject a previously captured SealedMessage byte-for-byte
can inject arbitrary numbers of unrelated valid messages to pressure the replay cache
prerequisites: an established session between two devices
at least one message delivered and opened by the receiver

oracle.success_means: the harness prints REPLAY_ACCEPTED, i.e. the second open() returned the plaintext (invariant broken)
oracle.negative_control: first open() of a fresh message must print OPEN_OK; if the harness cannot even open a legitimate message the run is INDETERMINATE, not a pass

severity_rationale: If replay succeeds, every downstream guarantee that assumes message-key uniqueness is void: duplicate delivery, forced re-execution of message-triggered actions, and a decryption oracle for probing. For a crypto library whose reason to exist is to replace libsignal safely, a replay hole is release-blocking (High/Critical).
